messages:
alex.support: Tina from Acme reporting 403s hitting our /v1/generate endpoint after they rotated their API key yesterday during a canary. Happening from a k8s job. They say 'works for a few minutes, then 403'. Can infra take a look? @sasha @kevin

sasha.eng-infra: ack, can you paste the root request_id and a tiny log snippet?

alex.support: request_id=rid-3a9f, log line: `2024-09-10T14:02:11Z ERROR auth: api key invalid for tenant=acme req=rid-3a9f`. Customer timeline: rotated key at 13:50, got successful calls until ~13:58 then errors.

kevin.eng-runtime: quick hypothesis: something serving cached creds (sidecar or init container) kept the old key, then the auth layer started rejecting once our auth cache invalidation hit other proxies. Do we know if they use Vault CSI or env var files?

alex.support: Tina says their CI writes the key into a k8s secret and an init-container copies it to /etc/creds/service.key (legacy flow). They didn't rotate the sidecar or restart the long-lived pods.

tina.customer: yes, we rotated via vaultctl rewrap then updated k8s secret, but our cron job didn't restart the main pods. we saw some success immediately after rotation (we have some short-lived jobs) then large fraction of 403s.

devops.oncall: can you run `kubectl get pods -o wide` and `kubectl exec` into one failing pod to show /etc/creds content? if the file is old that proves stale init copy.

kevin.eng-runtime: also check edge-proxy logs — if different nodes have different KMS aliases or if our auth service attempted to unwrap token with wrong KMS key alias it could reject. We had an incident where cross-region alias mismatch caused 403 for wrapped tokens.

alex.support: pasted customer's minimal repro they sent: ```
# on failing pod
cat /etc/creds/service.key
> sk_live_OLD_abc123
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_OLD_abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
> HTTP/1.1 403 Unauthorized\n{"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

sasha.eng-infra: thanks. alex, can you ask them to `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl get secret <name> -o yaml` to confirm secret updated? we need the timeline between secret update and pod restart.

tina.customer: secret shows new value, timestamp 2024-09-10T13:51:02Z. Pod was created at 2024-09-10T13:30:00Z. No recent rollout.

devops.oncall: that's the classic init-container copy got stale. Two recommended remediations: 1) rolling restart of the deployment so new pods pick up secret; 2) short-term fix: trigger a restart of the sidecar/agent that reads /etc/creds (if it's reload-capable). Which can you do?

tina.customer: we can trigger a rollout. doing `kubectl rollout restart deploy/service` now.

(5m later)

alex.support: update?

tina.customer: after rollout restart ~ 14:12, immediate reduction in 403s. Only a few leftover 403s from older jobs. Seems fixed. Thanks.

kevin.eng-runtime: follow-up note: we should verify they don't have cross-region KMS alias mismatch. Tina, was Vault transit configured with a KMS alias per region? any chance some wrapped tokens weren't rewrapped under new alias?

tina.customer: we are multi-region, but vaultctl rewrap was run in us-east only. some jobs still land on eu-west nodes because our scheduler spreads them. maybe those jobs tried to use the old wrapped tokens and hit mismatch.

vault-bot: Vault event: rewrap operation completed for secret/service at 2024-09-10T13:50:58Z in us-east-1. No eu-west rewrap recorded for that secret.

kevin.eng-runtime: okay that explains the intermittent success then failure pattern. Action items: - support: document repro & customer fix (rolling restart) - infra: recommend using Vault CSI or sidecar that reloads secrets so init-container copies aren't relied on - infra: check cross-region rewrap tooling and ensure rewrap runs for all regions or use a single global unwrapped store.

alex.support: I'll close the ticket once Tina confirms stable. Also will add note to KB: 'If you use init-container copy of secrets, rotate + rollout required'.

tina.customer: stable now, 0.2% 403s (background). we'll adopt CSI driver. thanks for quick help :thumbsup:

alex.support: filing follow-up doc and linking runbook to customer record. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
